title: Continuous Audit and Assurance
answer: Ledger anomaly detection, substantive testing, inventory observation, going concern analysis and controls testing.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Ledger Anomaly Detection
children.blurb: Ledger anomaly detection is the practice of scanning general ledger and subledger entries for items that depart from expected patterns, including duplicate postings, unusual account combinations, round amounts, odd posting times, and late top-side adjustments.

children.name: Substantive Testing at Full Coverage
children.blurb: Substantive testing at full coverage means applying audit procedures to every item in a defined population rather than to a sample.

children.name: Inventory Observation and Valuation
children.blurb: Inventory observation and valuation covers the evidence that inventory exists, is owned or controlled, is complete, is in saleable condition, and is carried at the right amount in the financial statements.

children.name: Going Concern Analysis
children.blurb: Going concern analysis in continuous audit and assurance is the ongoing evaluation of whether an entity can meet its obligations and continue operating for the foreseeable future.

children.name: Internal Control Testing
children.blurb: Internal control testing covers the design and operating effectiveness of controls that support reliable financial reporting, compliance and operations.

sections.body: Continuous audit and assurance is the use of AI to monitor accounting records, transactions, and controls on an ongoing basis rather than only at period end. In practice, AI systems scan ledgers for unusual patterns, flag duplicate payments, odd journal entries, and out-of-policy expenses. They can sample entire populations for substantive testing, compare invoices to contracts, and test controls by looking at approval trails and segregation of duties. In inventory, models combine counts, images, sensor data, and cost records to spot valuation problems. For going concern, AI reads filings, news, and cash flow trends to surface warning signs earlier. The work is assistive: auditors and accountants still set materiality, judge evidence, and sign conclusions.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some tasks are relatively mature, such as rule-based and machine learning anomaly detection on large transaction sets, and full population testing where data is clean and digital. Controls testing benefits from automation when logs are complete and access rights are well mapped. Inventory observation is harder because physical counts, condition, and obsolescence require judgment and often messy data. Going concern analysis remains difficult because it depends on forward-looking assumptions, management intent, and events that models cannot reliably predict. The honest limits are false positives, poor data quality, opaque model reasoning, and the need for audit trail and governance. AI can widen coverage and speed up review, but it does not remove professional skepticism or the need for corroborating evidence.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages in this section follow the audit workflow from records to conclusions. Ledger Anomaly Detection covers the entry point, where transactions are screened for outliers and possible misstatement. Substantive Testing at Full Coverage explains how AI moves beyond sampling to examine entire populations and gather evidence on balances and classes of transactions. Inventory Observation and Valuation deals with the physical and measurement problems that resist pure automation. Going Concern Analysis looks at the forward-looking assessment of an entity's ability to continue, where AI supports but cannot replace judgment. Internal Control Testing addresses the design and operating effectiveness of controls, including approvals, access, and exception handling, and the site's 222 compliance and regulation pages sit alongside this section for the wider rulebook.
